title: 2. Imperfect Diagnostic Tests, Latent-Class Coupling, and Subgroup Cohorts
text: LTBI diagnostic tests—interferon-gamma release assays (IGRA: QuantiFERON, T-SPOT.TB) tuberculin skin test (TST)—imperfect sensitivity specificity. Furthermore, clinical cohorts differ diagnostic test results active TB progression follow-structured: Population-Level vs. Individual-Level Latent-Class Coupling (coupling): Whether link population-level prevalence \(\pi\) across modules, jointly marginalize individual’s latent infection status \(Z_i \\{0, 1\}\) across baseline test result(s) \(\mathbf{x}_i\) progression outcome \((t_i, d_i)\). Single vs. Multiple Diagnostic Tests (\(K \ge 1\)): Combining \(K = 2\) tests (e.g., IGRA + TST) individuals provides conditional latent-class information sensitivity, specificity, prevalence. -Comers vs. Test-Positive Follow-(cohort_type): test-positive individuals (\(X_{,1} = 1\)) followed progression, false positives progress active TB, uncured fraction Positive Predictive Value (\(\text{PPV}\)) rather population prevalence \(\pi\). Covariates & Parametric Survival Families (covariates, surv_dist): Adjusting prevalence baseline risk factors comparing Gompertz, Weibull, Exponential progression hazards.

title: 2. Imperfect Diagnostic Tests, Latent-Class Coupling, and Subgroup Cohorts
text: Let \(Z_i \\{0, 1\}\) denote true baseline LTBI status individual \(\), covariate-adjusted prevalence: \[ P(Z_i = 1) = \pi_i = \text{logit}^{-1}(\eta_i), \qquad \eta_i = \alpha + \mathbf{x}_{\text{cov}, }^\top \boldsymbol{\beta}. \] Suppose individual \(\) undergoes \(K \ge 1\) diagnostic tests \(\mathbf{X}_i = (X_{,1}, \dots, X_{,K})\) sensitivities \(\text{sens}_k = P(X_{,k} = 1 \mid Z_i = 1)\) specificities \(\text{spec}_k = P(X_{,k} = 0 \mid Z_i = 0)\). Conditional \(Z_i\), test likelihood : \[ P(\mathbf{X}_i = \mathbf{x}_i \mid Z_i = 1) = \prod_{k=1}^{K} \text{sens}_k^{x_{,k}} (1 - \text{sens}_k)^{1 - x_{,k}}, \qquad P(\mathbf{X}_i = \mathbf{x}_i \mid Z_i = 0) = \prod_{k=1}^{K} (1 - \text{spec}_k)^{x_{,k}} \text{spec}_k^{1 - x_{,k}}. \] Marginalizing \(Z_i \\{0, 1\}\) gives marginal test likelihood individual \(\): \[ P(\mathbf{X}_i = \mathbf{x}_i) = (1 - \pi_i) P(\mathbf{X}_i = \mathbf{x}_i \mid Z_i = 0) + \pi_i P(\mathbf{X}_i = \mathbf{x}_i \mid Z_i = 1). \]

title: 2. Imperfect Diagnostic Tests, Latent-Class Coupling, and Subgroup Cohorts
text: Recognizes latent infection state \(Z_i \\{0, 1\}\) governs individual \(\)’s baseline test results \(\mathbf{x}_i\) ability progress active TB \((t_i, d_i)\). Marginalizing \(Z_i\) joint outcome \((\mathbf{X}_i, T_i, d_i)\) yields: \[ L_i^{\text{LC}}(\mathbf{x}_i, t_i, d_i) = \begin{cases} \pi_i \, P(\mathbf{x}_i \mid Z_i = 1) \, f_u(t_i) & \text{} d_i = 1 \text{ (active TB progression confirms } Z_i = 1\text{)}, \\[6pt] (1 - \pi_i) \, P(\mathbf{x}_i \mid Z_i = 0) + \pi_i \, P(\mathbf{x}_i \mid Z_i = 1) \, S_u(t_i) & \text{} d_i = 0 \text{ (right-censored } t_i\text{)}. \end{cases} \] Notice two critical properties \(L_i^{\text{LC}}\): 1. Every individual progresses active TB (\(d_i = 1\)) known certainty truly infected (\(Z_i = 1\)), baseline test result directly informs test sensitivity via \(P(\mathbf{x}_i \mid Z_i = 1)\). 2. Cut model (model = "cut", Stage 2) "latent_class" coupling, Stage 2 conditions censored person’s survival mixture individual test-updated posterior infection probability \(\text{PPV}(\mathbf{x}_i) = P(Z_i = 1 \mid \mathbf{x}_i)\): \[ \text{PPV}(\mathbf{x}_i) = P(Z_i = 1 \mid \mathbf{x}_i) = \frac{\pi_i \, P(\mathbf{x}_i \mid Z_i = 1)}{(1 - \pi_i) \, P(\mathbf{x}_i \mid Z_i = 0) + \pi_i \, P(\mathbf{x}_i \mid Z_i = 1)}. \]

title: 2. Imperfect Diagnostic Tests, Latent-Class Coupling, and Subgroup Cohorts
text: many clinical studies, individuals test positive baseline screening (\(X_{,1} = 1\)) enrolled longitudinal follow-. test specificity \(\text{spec}_1 < 1\), fraction test-positive individuals false positives (\(Z_i = 0, X_{,1} = 1\)) can never progress active TB. Bayes’ rule, effective uncured fraction \(\tilde{\pi}_i\) among test-positives Positive Predictive Value: \[ \tilde{\pi}_i = \text{PPV}_i = P(Z_i = 1 \mid X_{,1} = 1) = \frac{\pi_i \, \text{sens}_1}{\pi_i \, \text{sens}_1 + (1 - \pi_i)(1 - \text{spec}_1)}, \] survival mixture cure likelihood test-positive cohort becomes: \[ L_{\text{pos-}, }(t_i, d_i) = \left[ \text{PPV}_i \, f_u(t_i) \right]^{d_i} \left[ (1 - \text{PPV}_i) + \text{PPV}_i \, S_u(t_i) \right]^{1 - d_i}. \]

title: 1. Comparing Synthesis Models: Cut, Joint, Melding, Elastic, and Tempered Inference
text: tuberculosis (TB) epidemiology, often want combine two complementary sources evidence: Module 1 (\(M_1\), Starting State Occupancy / LTBI Survey Data \(Y_1\)): Cross-sectional screening diagnostic survey data informing baseline latent TB infection (LTBI) prevalence \(\pi_{\text{diag}} = \text{logit}^{-1}(\alpha_{\text{diag}})\) diagnostic test accuracy (\(\text{sens}, \text{spec}\)). Module 2 (\(M_2\), Active TB Progression Survival Data \(Y_2\)): Longitudinal follow-data \((t_i, d_i)_{=1}^{N_{\text{surv}}}\) informing uncured progression density \(f_u(t \mid \psi)\) survival \(S_u(t \mid \psi)\) (hazard parameters \(\psi = (\lambda, \gamma)\)) alongside survival cohort’s uncured LTBI fraction \(\pi_{\text{surv}} = \text{logit}^{-1}(\alpha_{\text{surv}})\). datasets represent underlying target population without selection bias (\(\pi_{\text{diag}} = \pi_{\text{surv}}\)), Joint model pools information across modules. However, longitudinal progression cohort suffers selection bias, case-mix differences, incomplete follow-(\(\pi_{\text{surv}} \neq \pi_{\text{diag}}\)), naive joint pooling allows biased survival data \(Y_2\) corrupt LTBI prevalence estimate \(\pi_{\text{diag}}\). EvidSynthTB provides six synthesis strategies ("joint", "cut", "independent", "melding", "elastic", "tempered") together quantitative comparison tools (compare_evidsynth(), evaluate_comparison(), diagnose_feedback()).

previous_headings: Mathematical Formulation of the Six Synthesis Models
title: 1. Comparing Synthesis Models: Cut, Joint, Melding, Elastic, and Tempered Inference
text: Let \(\phi = (\alpha_{\text{diag}}, \boldsymbol{\beta}, \text{sens}, \text{spec})\) denote Module 1 parameters, \(\pi_{\text{diag}} = \text{logit}^{-1}(\alpha_{\text{diag}})\). \(M\) aggregate survey studies \(y_m\) positive tests \(n_m\) individuals tested: \[ L_1(Y_1 \mid \phi) = \prod_{m=1}^{M} \binom{n_m}{y_m} p_{\text{pos}, m}^{y_m} (1 - p_{\text{pos}, m})^{n_m - y_m}, \qquad p_{\text{pos}, m} = \pi_{\text{diag}} \, \text{sens} + (1 - \pi_{\text{diag}})(1 - \text{spec}). \] Let \(\psi = (\lambda, \gamma)\) denote uncured survival parameters Module 2, uncured density \(f_u(t_i \mid \psi)\), uncured survival \(S_u(t_i \mid \psi)\), event indicator \(d_i \\{0, 1\}\) (\(1 = \text{progressed active TB}\), \(0 = \text{right-censored}\)), uncured fraction \(\pi_{\text{surv}} = \text{logit}^{-1}(\alpha_{\text{surv}})\). Since individuals without LTBI progress active TB baseline infection, Module 2 forms mixture cure model: \[ L_2(Y_2 \mid \alpha_{\text{surv}}, \psi) = \prod_{=1}^{N_{\text{surv}}} \left[ \pi_{\text{surv}} \, f_u(t_i \mid \psi) \right]^{d_i} \left[ (1 - \pi_{\text{surv}}) + \pi_{\text{surv}} \, S_u(t_i \mid \psi) \right]^{1 - d_i}. \]

previous_headings: Mathematical Formulation of the Six Synthesis Models
title: 1. Comparing Synthesis Models: Cut, Joint, Melding, Elastic, and Tempered Inference
text: Assumes \(\alpha_{\text{surv}} = \alpha_{\text{diag}} = \alpha\) (\(\pi_{\text{surv}} = \pi_{\text{diag}} = \pi\)) unrestricted bidirectional information flow \(Y_1\) \(Y_2\): \[ p_{\text{joint}}(\phi, \psi \mid Y_1, Y_2) \propto p(\phi) \, p(\psi) \, L_1(Y_1 \mid \phi) \, L_2(Y_2 \mid \alpha_{\text{diag}}, \psi). \]

title: 1. Comparing Synthesis Models: Cut, Joint, Melding, Elastic, and Tempered Inference
text: Following Plummer (2015), Cut distribution allows information flow forward reliable survey module \(M_1\) survival module \(M_2\), completely blocking feedback \(Y_2\) back \(\phi\): \[ p_{\text{cut}}(\phi, \psi \mid Y_1, Y_2) = p(\phi \mid Y_1) \, p(\psi \mid Y_2, \phi) = \frac{p(\phi) L_1(Y_1 \mid \phi)}{p(Y_1)} \cdot \frac{p(\psi) L_2(Y_2 \mid \alpha_{\text{diag}}, \psi)}{\int p(\psi') L_2(Y_2 \mid \alpha_{\text{diag}}, \psi') \, d\psi'}. \] Note integrating \(\psi\) yields exact Stage 1 marginal \(\int p_{\text{cut}}(\phi, \psi \mid Y_1, Y_2) \, d\psi = p(\phi \mid Y_1)\), regardless misspecified biased \(Y_2\) . EvidSynthTB, implemented via two-stage multiple-imputation HMC: Stage 1 samples \(\phi^{(s)} \sim p(\phi \mid Y_1)\) using ltbi_module.stan, Stage 2 samples \(\psi^{(s)} \sim p(\psi \mid Y_2, \phi^{(s)})\) conditional fixed \(\phi^{(s)}\).

title: 1. Comparing Synthesis Models: Cut, Joint, Melding, Elastic, and Tempered Inference
text: Summarizes Stage 1 information logit prevalence scale via normal portal summaries \((\hat{\mu}_m, \hat{\sigma}_m)\) combines Stage 2 mixture cure likelihood single joint model (\(\alpha_{\text{surv}} = \alpha_{\text{diag}} = \alpha\)): \[ p_{\text{meld}}(\alpha, \psi \mid \hat{\mu}, \hat{\sigma}, Y_2) \propto p(\alpha) \, p(\psi) \left[ \prod_{m=1}^{M} \mathcal{N}(\hat{\mu}_m \mid \alpha, \hat{\sigma}_m^2) \right] L_2(Y_2 \mid \alpha, \psi). \]

title: 1. Comparing Synthesis Models: Cut, Joint, Melding, Elastic, and Tempered Inference
text: Links diagnostic survival logit prevalences Gaussian hierarchical prior tuneable coupling standard deviation \(\tau > 0\) (tau_couple): \[ p_{\text{elastic}}(\phi, \alpha_{\text{surv}}, \psi \mid Y_1, Y_2) \propto p(\phi) \, p(\psi) \, L_1(Y_1 \mid \phi) \, \mathcal{N}(\alpha_{\text{surv}} \mid \alpha_{\text{diag}}, \tau^2) \, L_2(Y_2 \mid \alpha_{\text{surv}}, \psi). \] \(\tau \0\), \(\alpha_{\text{surv}} \\alpha_{\text{diag}}\) (Joint model). \(\tau \\infty\), \(\alpha_{\text{surv}}\) \(\alpha_{\text{diag}}\) decouple (Independent model).

title: 1. Comparing Synthesis Models: Cut, Joint, Melding, Elastic, and Tempered Inference
text: EvidSynthTB provides two dedicated functions compare models: Bias & RMSE: \[ \text{Bias}(\hat{\theta}) = \mathbb{E}[\theta \mid Y] - \theta_{\text{true}}, \qquad \text{RMSE}(\hat{\theta}) = \sqrt{\mathbb{E}\!\left[(\theta - \theta_{\text{true}})^2 \mid Y\right]}. \] Uncured Survival Curve Integrated Absolute Error (IAE) & Integrated RMSE (IRMSE): \[ \text{IAE} = \frac{1}{t_{\text{lim}}} \sum_{t=1}^{t_{\text{lim}}} \left| \hat{S}_u(t) - S_u^{\text{true}}(t) \right|, \qquad \text{IRMSE} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{t_{\text{lim}}} \sum_{t=1}^{t_{\text{lim}}} \left( \hat{S}_u(t) - S_u^{\text{true}}(t) \right)^2}. \] Feedback Shift (\(\Delta_{\text{fb}}\)): Measures strongly survival data pull diagnostic prevalence \(\pi_{\text{diag}}\) away zero-feedback "cut" baseline: \[ \Delta_{\text{fb}}(M) = \mathbb{E}_M[\pi_{\text{diag}} \mid Y_1, Y_2] - \mathbb{E}_{\text{cut}}[\pi_{\text{diag}} \mid Y_1]. \] Inter-Module Conflict (\(\Delta_{\text{prev}}\)): Evaluates discrepancy survival cure-fraction prevalence survey prevalence (informative "independent" "elastic" models): \[ \Delta_{\text{prev}} = \pi_{\text{surv}} - \pi_{\text{diag}}, \qquad P_{\text{conflict}} = P(\pi_{\text{surv}} > \pi_{\text{diag}} \mid Y_1, Y_2). \] Survival WAIC: Computed pointwise survival log-likelihood \(\ell_{}^{(s)} = \log L_{2,}(\theta^{(s)})\) across posterior draws \(s = 1, \dots, S\): \[ \text{WAIC}_{\text{surv}} = -2 \sum_{=1}^{N_{\text{surv}}} \left( \log \left( \frac{1}{S} \sum_{s=1}^{S} \exp(\ell_i^{(s)}) \right) - \text{Var}_{s}(\ell_i^{(s)}) \right). \]

title: 3. UK PREDICT-TB Case Studies: Reconstructed Survival & Linked Migrant Cohort
text: UK PREDICT-TB study (Abubakar et al., 2018) evaluated latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) screening subsequent progression active TB among recent migrants TB contacts UK. Depending data access, researchers typically encounter two different data structures study: Case Study — Published Aggregate Positivity + Reconstructed Kaplan-Meier IPD (load_abubakar_2018()): published paper, observe aggregate baseline IGRA positivity count (\(y = 1444\) positive \(n = 6380\) participants) together pseudo-individual survival times \((t_i, d_i)_{=1}^{6380}\) reconstructed digitizing published Kaplan-Meier curve (scripts/reconstruct-progression-data.R). digitized survival curve link individual test outcomes \(x_i\) individual times \(t_i\), unlinked two-module synthesis problem. Case Study B — Linked Individual-Level Migrant Cohort (load_predict_migrant()): individual-level migrant sub-cohort extract (cleaned_migrant_predict_data.RData), participant \(\) linked baseline test result \(x_i \\{0, 1\}\), follow-time \(t_i\), active TB progression indicator \(d_i \\{0, 1\}\), demographic covariates (age, age_z, ethnicity). enables individual-level latent-class coupling covariate regression.

what: Case Study A: Unlinked Aggregate Survey + Reconstructed Survival Cohort
title: 3. UK PREDICT-TB Case Studies: Reconstructed Survival & Linked Migrant Cohort
text: Let \(y = 1444\) \(n = 6380\) denote aggregate IGRA positivity data Module 1, let \((t_i, d_i)_{=1}^{N_{\text{surv}}}\) denote digitized progression times Module 2. imperfect IGRA sensitivity specificity (\(\text{sens} \sim \text{Beta}(a_{\text{sens}}, b_{\text{sens}})\), \(\text{spec} \sim \text{Beta}(a_{\text{spec}}, b_{\text{spec}})\)) Gompertz uncured progression hazard \(h_u(t) = \lambda e^{\gamma t}\): \[ \begin{aligned} y &\sim \text{Binomial}\!\left(n, \, \pi_{\text{diag}} \, \text{sens} + (1 - \pi_{\text{diag}})(1 - \text{spec})\right), \\[4pt] L_2(t_i, d_i \mid \pi_{\text{surv}}, \lambda, \gamma) &= \left[ \pi_{\text{surv}} \, \lambda e^{\gamma t_i} \exp\!\left(-\frac{\lambda}{\gamma}(e^{\gamma t_i} - 1)\right) \right]^{d_i} \left[ (1 - \pi_{\text{surv}}) + \pi_{\text{surv}} \exp\!\left(-\frac{\lambda}{\gamma}(e^{\gamma t_i} - 1)\right) \right]^{1 - d_i}. \end{aligned} \] active TB progression events full cohort rare (~1.5% 5 years) follow-heavily right-censored around 4–5 years, fitting Module 2 alone (model = "independent") separately identify cure fraction \(1 - \pi_{\text{surv}}\) Gompertz shape parameter \(\gamma < 0\) (governs quickly progression hazard decays time). Linking Module 1 Module 2 via "cut", "joint", "elastic" anchors uncured fraction \(\pi\) using diagnostic test data, allowing survival curve \(S_u(t)\) among LTBI-positive individuals identified.

text: linked migrant cohort, participant \(\) baseline age \(a_i\) (standardized \(\text{age}_{z,}\)), baseline test result \(x_i \\{0, 1\}\), survival outcome \((t_i, d_i)\). Individual baseline LTBI prevalence modeled : \[ \text{logit}(\pi_i) = \alpha + \beta_{\text{age}} \, \text{age}_{z,}. \] individual-level latent-class coupling (coupling = "latent_class"), participant’s latent infection status \(Z_i \sim \text{Bernoulli}(\pi_i)\) jointly governs \(x_i\) \((t_i, d_i)\): \[ L_i(x_i, t_i, d_i) = \begin{cases} \pi_i \, \text{sens}^{x_i} (1 - \text{sens})^{1 - x_i} \, f_u(t_i \mid \lambda, \gamma) & \text{} d_i = 1, \\[4pt] (1 - \pi_i) (1 - \text{spec})^{x_i} \text{spec}^{1 - x_i} + \pi_i \, \text{sens}^{x_i} (1 - \text{sens})^{1 - x_i} \, S_u(t_i \mid \lambda, \gamma) & \text{} d_i = 0. \end{cases} \]

title: 3. UK PREDICT-TB Case Studies: Reconstructed Survival & Linked Migrant Cohort
text: computational speed vignette, take stratified subsample including observed active TB events (\(d_i = 1\)) weighted sample censored observations (full analysis, scripts/script_Stan.R, pass abub$progression_data directly):   Notice Gompertz shape parameter \(\gamma\) (shape) estimated negative, reflecting biological reality hazard progressing LTBI active TB highest first 1–2 years entry/screening decays exponentially thereafter.
code: library(EvidSynthTB) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2)  abub <- load_abubakar_2018() abub$prevalence_data #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>       y     n test_id mu_hat sigma_hat #>   <int> <int>   <int>  <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1  1444  6380       1  -1.23    0.0299 head(abub$progression_data) #> # A tibble: 6 × 2 #>        t     d #>    <dbl> <int> #> 1 0.0601     1 #> 2 0.0601     1 #> 3 0.0601     1 #> 4 0.0601     1 #> 5 0.0601     1 #> 6 0.0601     1 set.seed(501) events_df <- dplyr::filter(abub$progression_data, d == 1L) cens_df <- dplyr::slice_sample(dplyr::filter(abub$progression_data, d == 0L), n = 450) prog_sub <- dplyr::bind_rows(events_df, cens_df)  comp_abub <- compare_evidsynth(   prevalence_data = abub$prevalence_data,   progression_data = prog_sub,   models = c("cut", "joint", "independent", "elastic"),   imperfect_test = TRUE,   surv_dist = "gompertz",   t_lim = 10,   chains = 1,   n_iter = 400,   n_burnin = 200,   n_cut_subsamples = 8,   seed = 501 )  knitr::kable(comp_abub$summary_table, digits = 3) knitr::kable(diagnose_feedback(comp_abub), digits = 3) plot_model_comparison(   comp_abub,   variables = c("prev_diag", "prev_cf", "lambda", "shape") ) plot_survival_comparison(comp_abub, type = "uncured")

what: Simulate synthetic LTBI diagnostic and TB progression survival data — create_fake_data
title: Simulate synthetic LTBI diagnostic and TB progression survival data — create_fake_data
text: Generates synthetic data Bayesian Multi-Parameter Evidence Synthesis (MPES) linking latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) diagnostic test data active TB progression time--event data. Supports imperfect diagnostic tests (`sens`, `spec`), multiple diagnostic tests per person, linked unlinked cohorts, test-positive subgroup follow-, covariates, prior/data conflict scenarios (`p_ltbi_surv != p_ltbi`).

title: Simulate synthetic LTBI diagnostic and TB progression survival data — create_fake_data
code: create_fake_data(   N_surv = 500,   n_survey = c(1000),   p_ltbi = 0.3,   p_ltbi_surv = NULL,   sens = 0.85,   spec = 0.95,   surv_dist = c("gompertz", "weibull", "exponential"),   shape = 0.1,   rate = 0.1,   t_censor = 10,   cohort_type = c("all", "pos_only"),   include_covariates = FALSE,   beta_cov = c(0.4, 0.6),   seed = NULL )

title: Simulate synthetic LTBI diagnostic and TB progression survival data — create_fake_data
text: N_surv Integer. Sample size progression survival cohort (`pos_only` filtering). Default `500`. n_survey Integer vector. Sample sizes aggregate LTBI prevalence surveys. Default `c(1000)`. p_ltbi Numeric `(0, 1)`. True baseline LTBI prevalence diagnostic survey population. Default `0.30`. p_ltbi_surv Numeric `(0, 1)` `NULL`. True baseline LTBI prevalence progression survival cohort. Defaults `p_ltbi` (conflict). Set different value (e.g., `0.60`) simulate selection bias / conflict survey survival modules. sens Numeric vector `(0, 1]`. Sensitivity diagnostic test `k = 1, ..., K`. Default `0.85`. spec Numeric vector `(0, 1]`. Specificity diagnostic test `k = 1, ..., K`. Default `0.95`. surv_dist Character. Parametric survival distribution uncured progression times: `"gompertz"`, `"weibull"`, `"exponential"`. shape Numeric. Shape parameter `"gompertz"` (can real) `"weibull"` (must positive). Ignored `"exponential"`. Default `0.1`. rate Numeric (`> 0`). Hazard rate / scale parameter `lambda`. Default `0.1`. t_censor Numeric (`> 0`). Maximum administrative follow-/ censoring time. Default `10`. cohort_type Character. Either `""` (screened individuals followed active TB progression) `"pos_only"` (individuals testing positive test 1 followed progression, false positives cured effective uncured fraction positive predictive value, PPV). include_covariates Logical. `TRUE`, simulates two baseline covariates (`age_z` `high_inc_origin`) affecting `logit(p_ltbi)`. beta_cov Numeric vector length 2 used `include_covariates = TRUE`. Default `c(0.4, 0.6)`. seed Optional integer random seed reproducibility.

title: Simulate synthetic LTBI diagnostic and TB progression survival data — create_fake_data
text: list components: `progression_data` Tibble individual-level survival follow-    (`t`, `d`, `z_true`, test results `x1`, ..., optional covariates). `prevalence_data` Tibble aggregate binomial survey data (`y`,     `n`, `test_id`) plus normal logit plug-summaries (`mu_hat`,     `sigma_hat`). `diagnostic_ipd` Tibble individual-level test results (`x1`, ...)     progression cohort. `truth` List true data-generating parameters (`p_ltbi`,     `p_ltbi_surv`, `sens`, `spec`, `ppv_surv`, `surv_dist`, `shape`,     `rate`, `cohort_type`).

what: Fit Bayesian Multi-Parameter Evidence Synthesis Model for LTBI and TB Progression — evidsynth_fit
title: Fit Bayesian Multi-Parameter Evidence Synthesis Model for LTBI and TB Progression — evidsynth_fit
text: Links latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) diagnostic test / survey data active TB progression time--event data using parametric mixture cure model CmdStan. Supports imperfect diagnostic tests (`sens`, `spec`), multiple tests per person, linked unlinked datasets, six modular synthesis strategies (`"joint"`, `"cut"`, `"independent"`, `"melding"`, `"elastic"`, `"tempered"`).

title: Fit Bayesian Multi-Parameter Evidence Synthesis Model for LTBI and TB Progression — evidsynth_fit
code: evidsynth_fit(   prevalence_data = NULL,   progression_data,   model = c("cut", "independent", "joint", "melding", "elastic", "tempered"),   coupling = c("population", "latent_class"),   cohort_type = c("all", "pos_only"),   surv_dist = c("gompertz", "weibull", "exponential"),   imperfect_test = FALSE,   covariates = NULL,   priors = list(),   tau_couple = 0.5,   w_temper = 0.5,   t_lim = 20,   chains = 2,   n_iter = 1000,   n_burnin = 500,   n_thin = 1,   n_cut_subsamples = 25,   seed = 123,   refresh = 0 )

title: Fit Bayesian Multi-Parameter Evidence Synthesis Model for LTBI and TB Progression — evidsynth_fit
text: prevalence_data Data frame tibble aggregate LTBI survey data (columns `y` `n`, optional `test_id`) /normal logit plug-summaries (`mu_hat` `sigma_hat`). Can `NULL` individual-level diagnostic test results `x` (`x1`, `x2`, ...) present `progression_data`. progression_data Data frame tibble time--event follow-data columns `t` (follow-time `> 0`) `d` (`1` = active TB progression, `0` = right-censored), plus optional individual diagnostic test columns (`x` `x1`, `x2`, ...) covariates. model Character. Synthesis model strategy: `"joint"` Full joint synthesis sharing baseline LTBI prevalence     (`alpha_surv = alpha_diag`). `"cut"` True two-stage Bayesian cut model (Plummer 2015): fits     Stage 1 LTBI diagnostic/survey data alone, propagates     posterior draws prevalence test accuracy Stage 2 survival     inference zero feedback survival prevalence. `"independent"` Disjoint modules separate independent     prevalence parameters `prev_diag` `prev_cf`. `"melding"` Two-stage normal portal approximation (`mu_hat`,     `sigma_hat` `logit(pi)`) combined progression survival     likelihood. `"elastic"` Hierarchical coupling     `logit(prev_cf) ~ Normal(logit(prev_diag), tau_couple)`. `"tempered"` Power-likelihood synthesis weighting progression     survival likelihood `w_temper` `(0, 1]`. coupling Character. diagnostic test results progression times coupled individual-level linked test data provided: `"population"` (modular population-level prevalence link) `"latent_class"` (individual-level marginalization person's latent LTBI state `Z_i`). cohort_type Character. `""` screened individuals followed progression (uncured fraction `prev_cf`), `"pos_only"` test-positive individuals followed (uncured fraction positive predictive value, `ppv_cf`). surv_dist Character. Parametric uncured survival family: `"gompertz"`, `"weibull"`, `"exponential"`. imperfect_test Logical. `TRUE`, estimates test sensitivity (`sens`) specificity (`spec`) `Beta(a_sens, b_sens)` `Beta(a_spec, b_spec)` priors. `FALSE`, fixes `sens_fixed` `spec_fixed`. covariates Optional character vector covariate column names `progression_data` include linear predictor `logit(pi_i)`. priors Named list prior hyperparameters overriding defaults (`mu_alpha`, `sigma_alpha`, `sigma_beta`, `mu_shape`, `sigma_shape`, `a_lambda`, `b_lambda`, `a_sens`, `b_sens`, `a_spec`, `b_spec`, `sens_fixed`, `spec_fixed`). tau_couple Numeric (`> 0`). Coupling standard deviation logit scale `model = "elastic"`. Default `0.5`. w_temper Numeric `[0, 1]`. Power-likelihood weight survival module `model = "tempered"`. Default `0.5`. t_lim Integer (`>= 1`). Maximum integer time horizon posterior predicted survival curves `S_pred[1:t_lim]`. Default `20`. chains Integer. Number MCMC chains. Default `2`. n_iter Integer. Total iterations per chain (post-warmup draws + `n_burnin`). Default `1000`. n_burnin Integer. Warmup iterations per chain. Default `500`. n_thin Integer. Thinning interval. Default `1`. n_cut_subsamples Integer. Number Stage 1 posterior draws propagate Stage 2 conditional HMC `model = "cut"`. Default `25`. seed Optional integer random seed. refresh Integer. CmdStan output refresh rate (`0` suppresses progress printing). Default `0`.

title: Fit Bayesian Multi-Parameter Evidence Synthesis Model for LTBI and TB Progression — evidsynth_fit
text: S3 list object class `"evidsynth_fit"` containing: `draws` `posterior::draws_df` data frame posterior samples     `prev_cf`, `prev_diag`, `ppv_cf`, `sens`, `spec`, `lambda`, `shape`,     `S_pred[1:t_lim]`. `summary` Posterior summary table produced     `posterior::summarise_draws()`. `fit` Underlying `CmdStanMCMC` object (Stage 1/2 fit objects     `"cut"`). `data` Constructed Stan data list. `model` Character name synthesis strategy. `surv_dist` Character name uncured survival distribution.

title: EvidSynthTB 0.2.0
text: Migrated Bayesian backend cmdstanr posterior modernized Stan models inst/stan/ (ltbi_module.stan evidsynth_modular.stan). compare_evidsynth(), plot_model_comparison(), plot_survival_comparison() added fit compare multiple synthesis strategies side--side. create_fake_data() implemented simulate linked unlinked LTBI diagnostic active TB progression survival cohorts imperfect tests (sens, spec), multiple tests per person, pos_only subgroup follow-, covariates, prior/data conflict scenarios. diagnose_feedback() evaluate_comparison() added quantify inter-module conflict, feedback shift relative cut model, survival WAIC, parameter bias/RMSE/coverage, survival curve integrated absolute error. evidsynth_fit() expanded support six modular synthesis strategies ("joint", "cut", "independent", "melding", "elastic", "tempered"), "population" "latent_class" coupling, "" "pos_only" progression cohorts, "gompertz", "weibull", "exponential" survival distributions. load_abubakar_2018() load_predict_migrant() added load reconstructed UK PREDICT-TB Kaplan-Meier dataset cleaned migrant cohort dataset. plot_progression() updated support uncured ("uncured") population mixture ("population") survival curves posterior::draws_df output.
